::: {.home-intro}
::: {.home-intro-copy}
I serve as Assistant Secretary in the Office of the Cabinet Secretary, under the
Office of the President of the Philippines. My work in policy analytics draws
on statistical methods, machine learning, natural language processing and
generative artificial intelligence, using semantic search, knowledge graphs
and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), including GraphRAG, to support
information retrieval and policy analysis.

I hold a BSc in Mathematics with First Class Honours from the [University of
Bristol](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/2027/maths/bsc-mathematics/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.
I have accepted a place at Johns Hopkins University on the pathway to the
[Master of Science in Artificial
Intelligence](https://ep.jhu.edu/programs/artificial-intelligence/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.
My intended coursework focuses on applied machine learning and AI systems;
my independent interests include recursive self-improvement.
My interests also include network science, combinatorics, and algebraic topology,
with applications in healthcare, industry and public policy.
:::

## Teaching

I teach [*Discrete Mathematics*](teaching/index.qmd) part-time at
[Bulacan State University](https://bulsu.edu.ph/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}'s
[Bustos](https://bulsu.edu.ph/academics/campus/Bustos){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
Campus. I previously taught *Mathematics in the Modern World*
and *Living in the IT Era* at the
[San Rafael](https://bulsu.edu.ph/academics/campus/San%20Rafael){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
Campus, and was a teaching assistant for *Mathematical Programming* at the
[University of Bristol School of Mathematics](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/maths/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.

## Writing

I write [*Calculated*](calculated/index.qmd), a weekly Saturday column for the
*Manila Bulletin*. The newspaper's [author
archive](https://mb.com.ph/author/rj-nieto){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
provides links to the published essays.

## Hobby

My hobby is [independent work in network science, mathematics and
AI](research/index.qmd). My current imaging project asks how
image-analysis methods respond when images are rotated, resized, poorly
exposed, or degraded by sensor noise, and whether those response patterns can
help identify acquisition problems. The work continues my University of Bristol dissertation,
*Computational Stability of Cubical Homology*; the
[thesis](https://github.com/reyjosephnieto/ph/blob/main/Nieto_TDA_Public_20260430.pdf){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
and [Python implementation](https://github.com/reyjosephnieto/ph){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
are publicly available.

I also study self-improving AI systems, with a particular interest in recursive
self-improvement.

## Earlier work

My earlier work spans technical writing, journalism, national broadcasting,
public affairs, government communications, and programme delivery. Further
details are available in my [CV](cv/index.qmd) and on
[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rjosephnieto/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.
